name: AppSidebar
label: App sidebar
description: Collapsible navigation rail whose sub-items open in a side panel beside it or an accordion beneath their row, with category headings and a profile section.

props.name: sections
props.description: Navigation sections

props.name: collapsibleSections
props.description:
Let the reader fold each titled section under its heading: the heading
becomes a toggle with a chevron, and the section's rows glide shut
beneath it. Every section starts open. A section is known by its
`id`, or its `category` when it has none, the key the fold state lists. The collapsed rail and the
phone drawer show every row whatever is folded, since neither shows
the headings.

props.name: collapsedSections
props.description: Controlled list of folded sections, by each section's `id` (its `category` when it has none). Needs `collapsibleSections`.

props.name: defaultCollapsedSections
props.description: Sections folded at first (uncontrolled), by `id` (else `category`). Needs `collapsibleSections`.

props.name: onCollapsedSectionsChange
props.description: Fires with the full new list of folded sections whenever a heading is pressed, in both controlled and uncontrolled modes.

props.name: profile
props.description: Profile data for the bottom section

props.name: activeKey
props.description: Key of the currently active item. When one of its children is the current page (`activeSubKey` or `activeTertiaryKey`), that child carries `aria-current` instead, and this row drops its fill while the child shows below it.

props.name: activeSubKey
props.description: Key of the currently active sub-item

props.name: activeTertiaryKey
props.description: Key of the currently active third-level item, listed in the side panel

props.name: subNav
props.description:
Where an item's sub-items show. `panel` (the default) opens a top-level
item's sub-items straight into the side panel, with their children as
the panel's accordion, and the collapsed rail shows each label under its
icon. `accordion` opens them under the row instead, and a sub-item's own
children open in a side panel as level 3. On small screens both modes
drill in inside the drawer instead.

props.name: defaultPanelOpen
props.description: Whether the side panel starts open when there is one to show

props.name: panelOpen
props.description: Controlled open state of the side panel

props.name: onPanelOpenChange
props.description: Called when the side panel opens or collapses

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Whether sidebar starts expanded

props.name: expanded
props.description: Controlled expanded state

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Callback when expand/collapse changes

props.name: collapsible
props.description:
Whether the reader can collapse the rail. `false` keeps it expanded: no
toggle, and a click on the rail opens nothing.

props.name: responsive
props.description:
How the rail decides between its rail and its drawer form. `viewport`
(the default) follows the window: the rail folds on entering the tablet
band and turns into the drawer at the mobile breakpoint. `container`
does the same by the width of the rail's parent, for a rail inside a
framed host. `rail` and `drawer` leave the decision to the host, which
measures its own room (a chat does, at its own widths). Every value but
`viewport` needs `fixed={false}`: the drawer then covers the parent, not
the page, and holds no page scroll lock.

props.name: drawerOpen
props.description: Controlled open state of the drawer form

props.name: defaultDrawerOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer form starts open (uncontrolled)

props.name: onDrawerOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer opens or closes, including every close of its own: the scrim, the close button, Escape, a destination row, and growing back into the rail form

props.name: foldForPanel
props.description:
Fold the rail to its icon form when the side panel opens and its parent
has too little room for the expanded rail, the panel and a readable
column beside them: under 1000px (the 280px rail, the 240px panel and a
480px column). For a rail in a narrow host, such as a chat.

props.name: keyLabels
props.description: Replaces any legend an item's `keys` hint is drawn with, such as `{ ctrl: 'Strg' }` for a German keyboard

props.name: onProfileMore
props.description: Callback when profile more button clicked

props.name: layout
props.description:
How the rail meets the page, one of the three app shell modes. `flush`
runs it edge to edge on the shell colour behind a hairline divider,
nothing raised. `floating` floats it off the viewport edges as a glass card:
inset with rounded corners, the translucent glass fill over a backdrop
blur, and the floating shadow (the inset defaults to 20px and is
overridable via the --ds-sidebar-float-inset custom property). `inset`
runs it flush on the app shell colour, beside a raised content surface
inset from the edges, as AppLayout's `inset` layout draws it. Inside a
host that marks itself a shell (AppLayout, a chat or template page), the
rail reads that host's mode from the shell recipe. Defaults to
`inset` (or `floating` while the deprecated `floating` is set).

props.name: floating
props.description: Floats the rail as a glass card, the same as `layout="floating"`.

props.name: fixed
props.description:
Pin the rail to the viewport. `true` (the default) fixes it to the
viewport's start edge at the viewport's height, with the side panel and
the phone drawer fixed beside it, as a full-page app wants. `false`
lays it out in its parent instead, for a framed preview or a layout that
is not the whole page: the parent is a flex row with a definite height,
the rail is its first item at the parent's height (sticky, so it holds
while the parent scrolls), and the content beside it gives way as the
rail expands and the side panel opens. On a phone the trigger, the scrim
and the drawer stay inside the parent too.

props.name: topSlot
props.description: Rendered under the logo row, above the nav; fades out while collapsed

props.name: persistentTopSlot
props.description: Keeps `topSlot` shown while collapsed instead of fading it, clipped by the sweeping rail as the nav rows are, for content that draws its own collapsed form: a switcher that holds its mark on the rail's axis and fades the rest. The slot carries `data-expanded`, so its content can key off the rail's state

props.name: footerSlot
props.description: Rendered above the profile block; fades out while collapsed

props.name: drawerTopEntries
props.description:
Rows above the sections in the phone drawer, in DrillMenu's shape, such
as a switcher that drills into its choices. When set, the drawer shows
these in `topSlot`'s place, since a dropdown has no room to open on a
full-screen menu.

props.name: drawerBottomEntries
props.description:
Rows after the sections in the phone drawer, in DrillMenu's shape, such
as appearance settings that drill into their choices. When set, the
drawer shows these in `footerSlot`'s place.

props.name: footerAction
props.description:
One primary action at the rail's foot, below the profile and full width,
as the site header's drawer pins its call to action: in the expanded
rail and the phone drawer alike, where it stays in view while the
levels above it scroll. The collapsed rail has no room for it, so it
fades out with the labels and is inert.

props.name: collapsedFooterSlot
props.description: Rendered above the profile block while the rail is collapsed, in `footerSlot`'s place: the same controls at their smallest, such as a SegmentedControl's or ThemeToggle's `cycle` circle, stacked and centred on the rail's axis. The two forms share one cell and crossfade with the rail, and whichever is hidden is inert

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component its links render with, such as Next.js's `Link`, so they
navigate through the app's router. Wins over a LinkProvider's; a plain
`<a>` when neither is set.

props.name: logo
props.description: Logo element — defaults to the built-in brand mark

props.name: logoText
props.description: Text shown next to logo when expanded

props.name: showMobileTrigger
props.description:
Below the mobile breakpoint the rail hides and this fixed hamburger
button opens it as an overlay drawer instead. Set false when the
host renders its own trigger in the page chrome.

props.name: openLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the mobile hamburger trigger that opens the drawer

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the toggle when it closes the mobile drawer

props.name: expandLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the toggle (and the collapsed logo) when it expands the rail

props.name: collapseLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the toggle when it collapses the rail

props.name: profileMoreLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the profile block's more button

props.name: menuLabel
props.description:
The phone drawer's menu: the accessible name of its navigation, and what
the back row says on every second level

props.name: drawerBackLabel
props.description:
The phone drawer's back row's accessible name, given the title of the level it
returns to, for a site in another language. The drill menu's own default.

props.name: drawerOverviewLabel
props.description:
The text of the overview row a drilled level opens with when its row has
a page of its own, given that row's label, for a site in another
language. The drill menu's own default.

AppSidebarLayout.description: The three app shell modes, how the rail meets the page: edge to edge behind a hairline, floating as a card, or flush beside a raised inset surface.

AppSidebarResponsive.description: How the rail decides between its rail and drawer forms.

AppSidebarSectionAction.description: A button in a section's heading, such as a project list's add.

AppSidebarSectionContext.description: What a section's `content` function is told about where it is drawn.

DrillMenuEntry.description: An entry on a level: a row, or a section of rows.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.

Shortcut.description: A shortcut in the grammar above, such as `mod+k`, `shift+?` or `g i`.

ShortcutKeyLabels.description: The legends a shortcut is drawn with, by modifier or key name. Merged over the platform's defaults.

keys.note: In its drawer form (below the mobile breakpoint, or when its host asks) the rail is a modal drawer: opening moves focus inside, Tab stays inside, and Escape closes it.

alternatives.name: ThreadPanel
alternatives.when: a standalone chat history rail is enough, one that renders on the server
